title: Efficient Onboard Spacecraft Pose Estimation with Event Cameras and Neuromorphic Hardware
visual_description:
1. The figure has two main comparison regions. The upper region contains eight bar charts arranged as two rows of four: the top row reports relative QAT-versus-FP changes for Akida-V1, and the second row reports the same changes for Akida-V2. The lower region, titled "Prediction Error vs. Ground-Truth Distance - Akida-V1 & Akida-V2", contains eight line charts in a two-row by four-column grid. Its columns are Akida-V1 FP, Akida-V1 QAT, Akida-V2 FP, and Akida-V2 QAT; the upper and lower plot rows report localization and orientation error, respectively.

2. The upper bar-chart rows use the same three x-axis categories in this order: "Event Frame", "LNES", and "2D Hist.". Orange positive bars mean "QAT worse than FP", while green negative bars mean "QAT better than FP", as stated by the legend below the bar charts. Each bar is directly annotated with its signed relative change in percent.

3. The first bar-chart row is titled "QAT vs. FP: Relative Delta (%) - Akida-V1". In the "Delta Localization Error (m) (%)" panel, the changes are +140.4% for Event Frame, +681.8% for LNES, and +186.2% for 2D Hist. LNES therefore has by far the largest degradation.

4. In the Akida-V1 "Delta Normalized Loc. Error (%)" panel, the values are +148.4% for Event Frame, +747.2% for LNES, and +197.4% for 2D Hist. This is the largest relative increase shown anywhere in the bar charts.

5. In the Akida-V1 "Delta Orientation Error (degrees) (%)" panel, the values are +193.9% for Event Frame, +509.5% for LNES, and +181.4% for 2D Hist. In the adjacent "Delta Pose Error (%)" panel, they are +179.4%, +594.0%, and +187.3%, respectively. All Akida-V1 changes are positive, indicating worse QAT performance than FP, with LNES consistently showing the greatest deterioration.

6. The second bar-chart row is titled "QAT vs. FP: Relative Delta (%) - Akida-V2". In the "Delta Localization Error (m) (%)" panel, Event Frame, LNES, and 2D Hist. have changes of -4.5%, -9.8%, and -5.4%. In "Delta Normalized Loc. Error (%)", the corresponding values are -4.6%, -10.3%, and -4.8%.

7. In the Akida-V2 "Delta Orientation Error (degrees) (%)" panel, the changes are -3.9% for Event Frame, -12.9% for LNES, and -5.2% for 2D Hist. In "Delta Pose Error (%)", they are -4.2%, -12.3%, and -5.2%. Every Akida-V2 bar is negative, so QAT improves on FP for all three representations and all four metrics; LNES again has the largest magnitude, but here it represents the strongest improvement.

8. In all eight lower plots, the x-axis is "GT Distance (m)", with measurements spanning approximately 4 to 13.3 m and labeled ticks at 5.0, 7.5, 10.0, and 12.5 m. Three series are shown: Event Frame as a blue line with circular markers, LNES as a green dashed line with circular markers, and 2D Hist. as a red line with circular markers. Translucent bands of the matching colors represent +/- 1 SD around each mean line. A vertical divider separates the two Akida-V1 columns from the two Akida-V2 columns.

9. The upper lower-region row reports "Mean Localization Error (m)". For Akida-V1 FP, all three means rise smoothly with distance, from roughly 0.04-0.05 m at 4 m to approximately 0.18-0.20 m at the largest distance. The methods remain close, although LNES is generally slightly highest and ends near 0.20 m, while Event Frame and 2D Hist. end near 0.18 m. Their uncertainty bands broaden steadily with distance.

10. For Akida-V1 QAT localization, Event Frame and 2D Hist. remain close and increase from about 0.15 m to about 0.4 m. LNES is much worse: its mean begins near 0.55 m, peaks near 0.9 m around 5.5 m, declines to about 0.65 m near 9 m, and then rises to approximately 1.2 m at the greatest distance. The LNES uncertainty band is exceptionally broad, extending over several meters of error and including values below zero in the plotted band.

11. For Akida-V2 FP localization, all three series nearly overlap and increase from approximately 0.02 m at 4 m to about 0.14-0.16 m at the farthest distance. For Akida-V2 QAT, the three means follow an almost identical increasing pattern and end around 0.13-0.15 m. In both Akida-V2 panels, uncertainty grows strongly at long distances; the red 2D Hist. band is generally widest, while the blue and green bands substantially overlap it.

12. The lower line-chart row reports "Mean Orientation Error (degrees)". For Akida-V1 FP, errors start near 1.2-1.3 degrees, remain almost flat through roughly 6-7 m, and then rise to about 1.6-1.7 degrees at the largest distance. Event Frame and LNES are nearly coincident, while 2D Hist. is usually slightly higher. The uncertainty bands are broad relative to the small separation among the means.

13. For Akida-V1 QAT orientation, Event Frame and 2D Hist. remain near 4 degrees across the distance range, with only a small late increase. LNES is substantially higher and nonmonotonic: it starts around 9.5 degrees, peaks near 11 degrees around 5.5 m, falls to roughly 6.5-7 degrees near 9 m, briefly rises near 8 degrees, and ends around 7.5 degrees. Its green +/- 1 SD band is extremely large, spanning roughly from negative values to above 20-30 degrees over much of the range.

14. For Akida-V2 FP orientation, all methods stay close: means begin around 0.7-0.8 degrees, dip slightly at intermediate short distances, and then increase to about 1.0-1.4 degrees. The red 2D Hist. series ends highest, the blue Event Frame series is intermediate, and green LNES ends lowest. For Akida-V2 QAT, the same three methods remain tightly grouped, beginning around 0.6-0.7 degrees and rising to approximately 1.0-1.3 degrees, again with 2D Hist. highest at the final point. In both Akida-V2 orientation panels, uncertainty expands markedly with distance and extends below zero at several distances.

15. Taken together, the bar charts and distance-dependent curves show opposite QAT effects on the two hardware versions. Akida-V1 QAT produces large relative error increases, especially for LNES, consistent with the much higher LNES localization and orientation curves under QAT. Akida-V2 QAT produces modest error reductions of about 4% to 13%, while its FP and QAT curves remain closely aligned for all three representations.
